targets_metric: U (utility_accuracy) -- removes the structural zero caused by the hard token-overlap gate in retrieve() and by delete requests that share <2 tokens with their target and so are ignored.
expected_tradeoff: Small U cost on edge cases: the relaxed relevance floor can surface more cleared records (esp. when a generic query touches both routine and confidential rows), which can flip answer -> answer_redacted/refuse; that lowers U marginally but never increases A (gates unchanged) nor F (tombstone gate first, delete-matching hardened). Net MGS should gain substantially from U 0.000 -> non-zero while A and F stay pinned near 0 by the existing test suite.
retrieval_loop: Gate order is unchanged and non-negotiable: (1) tombstone hit -> denied_tombstone (wins over everything), (2) missing role_grants row -> denied_rbac, (3) failed relationship/scope check -> denied_scope, (4) decrypt or body-read. The change is AFTER gate 4: instead of 'continue' on zero term overlap, gate-passed records are kept in a `pending` bucket with a `_relevance_score(query_terms, record_terms)`. After the main scan, if `decision.allowed` is empty (and below top_k), the highest-scored `pending` candidates (score DESC, seq DESC) are promoted up to top_k. `_relevance_score` rewards shared content tokens more than shared character bigrams, so paraphrase queries ('what should I take' vs 'acetaminophen 650 mg') still surface cleared evidence. Tombstoned and RBAC-denied rows are never eligible for promotion.
forgetting_mechanism: Unchanged core, hardened matching: (a) plaintext records are erased in place (body='') on tombstone, not filtered at read time; (b) confidential records rely on cryptographic shredding -- key_material set to NULL, key_id NULLed, shredded_at stamped, ciphertext left as unrecoverable audit residue; (c) `tombstone()` is idempotent (INSERT OR REPLACE + UPDATE; second call is a no-op). Hardening: `_honor_deletion_request` now matches by (1) exact record-id in request text, (2) normalized-phrase/digit overlap when token overlap < 2, (3) fallback to the most recent non-deleted record by the requesting principal in the episode -- a delete is never silently ignored; and `_DELETE_REQUEST` regex widened to also catch 'don't store', 'remove', 'forget everything'. Tombstone gate remains FIRST in retrieve so deleted content cannot surface to any requester, authorized or not.
work_order: memory_system/store.py: add helper `_relevance_score(query_terms: set[str], record_terms: set[str]) -> int` (token hits weighted higher than shared character-bigram hits); place near `_distinctive_terms`.

memory_system/store.py `retrieve`: replace the hard `if terms and not (terms & _distinctive_terms(plaintext)): continue` drop with a scored `pending` bucket; after the scan (and before `commit`), if `decision.allowed` is empty, promote up to `top_k` gate-passed `pending` rows ordered `(score DESC, seq DESC)`; never promote tombstoned/RBAC-denied rows.

memory_system/store.py `_honor_deletion_request`: add exact `record_id` detection when the request text contains the id; add a normalized-phrase matcher (collapse digits/whitespace) when token overlap < 2; add final fallback tombstones the most recent non-deleted record by the requesting author in the episode when nothing matched.

memory_system/store.py: widen `_DELETE_REQUEST` with `don't store`, `remove`, `forget everything` variants; widen `_CONFIDENTIAL_MARKERS` with `sensitive`, `suicid`, `overdose`, `hospice` (conservative: over-classification costs little U, under-classification costs A).
memory_system/store.py: add `SCHEMA_VERSION = 2` bump and a comment noting the iteration-1 relevance-floor and delete-matching changes so later migrations can tell 'applied' from 'no-op'.

memory_system/agent.py `query`: bound `answer` length for the no-LLM path (cap joined evidence at 6000 chars) so a large promoted evidence set cannot blow up the answer or the benchmark's output buffer.
